messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: adaptation, exceptions and NaN;  this -> _foo;  static_cast<bar>(...) vs. bar(...)
parts:
I didn't see anything in place to handle the exceptional
returns and NaN returns possible when evaluating log probabilities
during adaptation.

I'm worried about examples like the following in init_stepsize() in
base_hmc.hpp:

if ((direction == 1) && !(delta_H > log(0.5)))
break;

If delta_H is NaN, then !(delta_H > log(0.05)) will be true, and we
break out of the loop with a bad value and no warning.

Could we instead check if we get a NaN response or exception and
perhaps report something back to the user by throwing an exception
with an appropriate message? Or, if we want to treat it as 0 probability,
treating it like 0 probability?

- Bob

P.S. I'm also very distracted by all the uses of (this->_foo) for
member variables _foo. You shouldn't need the "this->" part.
(I know we had some trouble getting things to compile for at
least one instance, and I'd still like to figure out what was
wrong there.)

P.P.S. You don't need static casts like this one in base_hmc.hpp:

ps_point z_init(static_cast<ps_point>(this->_z));

If you have a non-pointer type like the class ps_point, then

static_cast<ps_point>(foo)

is just longhand for

ps_point(foo)

So you'll ge the same result with

ps_point z_init(ps_point(_z));

and thus with

ps_point z_init(_z);
